pr_title: sys/time_units.h: Work around clang div-by-zero warning
pr_body:
clang emits a warning for this code:

  foo.c:1:25: warning: division by zero is undefined [-Wdivision-by-zero]
  int i = (10 > 100 ? (20 / (10 / 100)) : (20 * (100 / 10)));
	                        ^ ~~~~~~~~~~

The warning is generated for code whose value does not affect the expression result, but technically it is still 'undefined behavior'.

Work around this warning by checking for a zero divisor and substituting one to make the compiler happy.

Closes: #63564
pr_comments:
> Can we add a test-case which triggers this issue to `tests/kernel/timer/timer_api/src/timer_convert.c`?

good idea. That also caught a problem with the definition of Z_HZ_cyc, which used sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec. That was never a constant expression because it was a static inline instead of being a macro.

> That also caught a problem with the definition of Z_HZ_cyc, which used sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec. That was never a constant expression because it was a static inline instead of being a macro.

Hmm, do we require that sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec must be compile-time constant?

Cause it naturally can't be compile-time constant if `CONFIG_TIMER_READS_ITS_FREQUENCY_AT_RUNTIME` is enabled - so we use `sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec_runtime_get()`

> > That also caught a problem with the definition of Z_HZ_cyc, which used sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec. That was never a constant expression because it was a static inline instead of being a macro.
> 
> Hmm, do we require that sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec must be compile-time constant?

No, it's only constant when it isn't read at runtime. The issue was that `sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec()` wasn't a "constant" even when the timer frequency was specified at compile time.

> Cause it naturally can't be compile-time constant if `CONFIG_TIMER_READS_ITS_FREQUENCY_AT_RUNTIME` is enabled - so we use `sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec_runtime_get()`

Yup. In that case, we aren't testing to make sure the timer macros are valid C constant expressions.

> > That also caught a problem with the definition of Z_HZ_cyc, which used sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec. That was never a constant expression because it was a static inline instead of being a macro.
> 
> Hmm, do we require that sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec must be compile-time constant?
> 
> Cause it naturally can't be compile-time constant if `CONFIG_TIMER_READS_ITS_FREQUENCY_AT_RUNTIME` is enabled - so we use `sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec_runtime_get()`

I'm wondering if this means we need something like #63594 ? As far as I can tell, this only impacts qemu_x86 platforms (as those appear to use HPET which implies run-time timer freq).
@evgeniy-paltsev can you revisit this once you have a chance? Would be nice to merge it before RC2.

> @evgeniy-paltsev can you revisit this once you have a chance? Would be nice to merge it before RC2.

@andyross (as the assignee) would also need to approve first

> As far as I can tell, this only impacts qemu_x86 platforms (as those appear to use HPET which implies run-time timer freq).

FWIW: I wouldn't cry if someone went in there with a hatchet and just removed the runtime frequency query from the HPET driver.  Literally everything else in Zephyr is based on compile-time hardware configuration, and in point of fact all of our HPET x86 devices have hard frequency settings anyway, IIRC.

CONFIG_TIMER_READS_ITS_FREQUENCY_AT_RUNTIME is a historical wart, and it doesn't even do the thing we actually know we need, which is dynamic runtime frequency selection (right now there are a handful of devices that do that, but by translation inside the timer driver).

> CONFIG_TIMER_READS_ITS_FREQUENCY_AT_RUNTIME is a historical wart, and it doesn't even do the thing we actually know we need, which is dynamic runtime frequency selection (right now there are a handful of devices that do that, but by translation inside the timer driver).

I'd suspect to make this work reliably you'd need to annotate every timeout value with some kind of 'required precision' value so that the dynamic frequency stuff didn't introduce so much slop that things started breaking when the core timer frequency got set too low...

In any case, it looks like HPET doesn't require runtime timer values, it just allows them, so turning all of that off could be done by simply removing the 'imply y' value from the relevant Kconfig file.

issue_context.title: Spurious `warning: division by zero is undefined` on `K_THREAD_DEFINE` when building with clang
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Hi, bumped into this compiler warning on `K_THREAD_DEFINE` since https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/62900 got merged. One of our project that is building for an stm32 with LLVM started failing with a compiler warning:

```
/mnt/host/source/src/platform/ec/zephyr/shim/src/tasks.c:51:1251: error: division by zero is undefined [-Werror,-Wdivision-by-zero]

((k_ticks_t) -1) : ((k_ticks_t)((1) ? ( ((10000) == (1000)) ? (uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) : ((1000) > (10000) && (1000) % (10000) == 0U) ? ((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) + ((0) ? ((1000) / (10000)) / 2 : (1) ? ((1000) / (10000)) - 1 : 0)) / ((1000) / (10000)) : ((10000) > (1000) && (10000) % (1000) == 0U) ? (uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0)))*((10000) / (1000)) : ((((((365 * 24ULL * 3600ULL * 1000) + (4294967295U) - 1) / (4294967295U)) * 10000) <= 4294967295U) ? (((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0)))*(10000) + ((0) ? (1000) / 2 : (1) ? (1000) - 1 : 0)) / (1000)) : (((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) / (1000))*(10000) + (((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) % (1000))*(10000) + ((0) ? (1000) / 2 : (1) ? (1000) - 1 : 0)) / (1000))) ) : (((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) / (1000))*(10000) + (((uint64_t) (((((-1)) > (0)) ? ((-1)) : (0))) % (1000))*(10000) + ((0) ? (1000) / 2 : (1) ? (1000) - 1 : 0)) / (1000)) ))) }), .init_name = "RWSIG", }; const k_tid_t RWSIG = (k_tid_t)&_k_thread_obj_RWSIG;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  ^ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

The cause seems to be the introduction of `SYS_TIMEOUT_MS` in `Z_THREAD_INITIALIZER`, the macro eventually expands into some call of `z_tmcvt_64` which includes a `/ (Z_HZ_ms / Z_HZ_cyc)`, that becomes a `/ 0` in most tickless setups since `Z_HZ_ms = 1000` and `Z_HZ_cyc = CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC = 10000`. The ternary picks the valid value and GCC is happy with that, but clang seems to be firing a warning.

I managed to reproduce this with this example:

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int ticks = 0 ? 1 / 0 : 0 ;

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
        printf("%d\n", ticks);
}
```

```
$ gcc -Wall -o test test.c
$ clang -Wall -o test test.c
test.c:3:19: warning: division by zero is undefined [-Wdivision-by-zero]
int ticks = 0 ? 1 / 0 : 0 ;
                  ^ ~
1 warning generated.
```

Note that for some reason the warning does not fire if the condition is moved inside the function.

The CI did not catch it because the clang build that we run is all for `native_posix` and runs with `SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC = 100`, but this can be reproduced upstream fairly easily with:

```
$ export ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=llvm
$ west build -p -b native_posix_64 samples/basic/threads -DCONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=10000
...
/usr/local/google/home/fabiobaltieri/zephyrproject/zephyr/samples/basic/threads/src/main.c:111:1: warning: division by zero is undefined [-Wdivision-by-zero]
K_THREAD_DEFINE(blink0_id, STACKSIZE, blink0, NULL, NULL, NULL,
^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
...
```

To get around this in our application we ended up selectively disabling the warning (https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/4907933), but that's obviously not a scalable workaround. Unfortunately the way our CI is setup does not give us much visibility into it, but there's probably many users compling with clang for tickless systems and I think this should be looked into before the release.

I tried to look into the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/include/zephyr/sys/time_units.h definitions but can't quite see a decent workaround, looking for more ideas around this.

**To Reproduce**
```
$ export ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=llvm
$ west build -p -b native_posix_64 samples/basic/threads -DCONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=10000
```

**Expected behavior**
No warning

**Impact**
Build fail if warning as treated as errors.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain: clang 14.0.6 and 17.0.0

I'll open a PR see if that would pass CI.

The logic *should* be using a multiply instead of divide for this case -- `* (Z_HZ_cyc / Z_HZ_ms)` instead of `/ (Z_HZ_ms / Z_HZ_cyc)`. Sounds like it should also be fairly easy to fix once I figure out why it did the wrong thing :-)

> The logic _should_ be using a multiply instead of divide for this case -- `* (Z_HZ_cyc / Z_HZ_ms)` instead of `/ (Z_HZ_ms / Z_HZ_cyc)`. Sounds like it should also be fairly easy to fix once I figure out why it did the wrong thing :-)

Ok it looks like there's more into it -- I closed https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/63580, will let you come up with the right fix before I mess things up even more. :-)

As far as I can determine, the compiler is complaining about a divide-by-zero in a branch *which will not be taken*.

Take a look at this code:
```
int i = (10 > 100 ? (20 / (10 / 100)) : (20 * (100 / 10)));
```

```
$ clang -c -O2 -Wall -Wextra foo.c
foo.c:1:25: warning: division by zero is undefined [-Wdivision-by-zero]
int i = (10 > 100 ? (20 / (10 / 100)) : (20 * (100 / 10)));
                        ^ ~~~~~~~~~~
1 warning generated.
```
I've submitted a PR which works around the warning by using 1 when the value would be zero. It cannot affect the result
because this code is in a conditional branch where from_hz (1000) is strictly greater than to_hz (10000).

> As far as I can determine, the compiler is complaining about a divide-by-zero in a branch _which will not be taken_.

Yes that is the case in my tests (the build fails with a different error if that branch is taken), and from my understanding the condition it cannot be taken in any case.

> As far as I can determine, the compiler is complaining about a divide-by-zero in a branch which will not be taken.

Exactly!

To me this looks like a bug in CLang: See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18385020/can-code-that-will-never-be-executed-invoke-undefined-behavior

> To me this looks like a bug in CLang: See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18385020/can-code-that-will-never-be-executed-invoke-undefined-behavior

Yeah, thinking about this again, the C 'short circuit' rules apply to the conditional operator which means that the undefined operation (divide by zero) will not happen, and hence the program is not invoking undefined behavior.

It's no different from using an if statement to protect the division operation.

> It's no different from using an if statement to protect the division operation.

I'd bet they'll come back with chapter-and-verse from the standard explaining why the compiler should work this way. That's the usual result of filing compiler issues.

review_comments: At what level of the language standard did that ternary syntax appear?  I worry because we have `__clang__` compilers in the stable (c.f. Cadence's xt-clang) which are comparatively old.  Might be safer to write that out long hand?  Or not, if we're sure this is supported.
Also grade school math pedantry: the operation of this macro should probably be named "quotient", or just "divide", the "divisor" is the `a` argument.

Yeah, the name actually refers to the division that this value is used as a part of -- which is in the `z_tmcvt_int_div_*` macros. In that context, it looks like I guessed right in using 'divisor' (I admit that I just checked :-)

> At what level of the language standard did that ternary syntax appear? 

Just for the record and the link, Elvis operator / GNU extension `?:` dropped in:
